deck: Supply chain issues and market shifts are reshaping defense and space.

stories.head: Missile production faces solid rocket motor bottleneck
stories.body: A CSIS report indicates that solid rocket motor production is struggling, potentially jeopardizing missile interceptor plans slated for 2027. This bottleneck underscores the fragility of defense supply chains, where one hiccup could derail entire programs. With the U.S. defense budget already under scrutiny, this isn't just a technical issue; it's a political hot potato.
stories.soWhat: If the military can’t get its missiles in time, expect a lot of finger-pointing and budget reallocations. Supply chain woes are the real enemy here.

stories.head: SpaceX shares jump nearly 20% on IPO debut
stories.body: In a notable market debut, SpaceX shares surged almost 20% on their first trading day, reaching a valuation of approximately $470 billion. This milestone not only reflects investor confidence in the commercial space sector but also sets a benchmark for other space firms eyeing public markets. For context, this is the largest IPO in the space industry to date, further legitimizing the sector as a profitable venture.
stories.soWhat: This surge might just be a flash in the pan, but it indicates that investors are ready to bet big on space—if they can find the right ticket.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris join forces for SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation, signaling a strategic alliance in a highly competitive landscape. This collaboration comes at a time when the U.S. is ramping up its space capabilities, with the FY27 budget earmarking an additional $1.4 billion for space resilience. As the defense sector shifts towards more integrated solutions, partnerships like this could redefine competitive dynamics.
stories.soWhat: In a game where alliances might matter more than tech, this partnership could be a harbinger of how future contracts are won—or lost.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX's secondary market moves
watchlist.body: With shares soaring, secondary market activity around SpaceX could heat up, impacting valuations across the sector.

watchlist.title: Implications of GPS jamming in Eastern Med
watchlist.body: With GPS jamming returning to pre-2024 levels, expect heightened scrutiny on navigation technologies and their vulnerabilities.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension could signal more contracts
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program could attract attention from other agencies looking for similar long-term commitments.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C could shift co-orbital dynamics
watchlist.body: With $190 million raised, True Anomaly may disrupt the co-orbital security landscape, especially as defense needs evolve.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
